Created `validate_email.py` with an `is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool` function.

```python
import re

EMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+"
    r"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?"
    r"(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)+$"
)

def is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool:
    if not email or len(email) > 254:
        return False
    return bool(EMAIL_PATTERN.match(email))
```

It checks: valid local-part characters, a proper domain with at least one dot, valid label lengths (≤63 chars), and an overall length cap of 254 (RFC 5321 limit). Ran it against sample cases (`<email>`, `invalid@`, `@example.com`, `user@.com`, etc.) and it correctly classified all of them.

Note: this covers the common 99% case but isn't a full RFC 5322 parser (e.g., it won't accept quoted local-parts or IP-literal domains). If you need stricter validation, `email-validator` (PyPI) is the standard library for that.
